findings.description: SQL injection: `name` is interpolated into the query with an f-string. An input like `' OR '1'='1` or a UNION payload returns or exposes arbitrary data. Use a parameterized query instead, e.g. `conn.execute("... WHERE name LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

`count // per_page` uses floor division, so a partial last page is not counted. 25 items with per_page=20 returns 1 instead of 2, which hides the remaining items. Use ceiling division: `(count + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

`getUser` is async (it is awaited in `getProjects`), but it is called here without `await`. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined and every request gets a 403, including requests from admins. Deleting a project never works.

The admin check for a destructive action relies on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user id can delete any project. A missing or unknown id also leaves `user` null or undefined, so `user.isAdmin` throws.

spurious.description: The admin check for a destructive action relies on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user id can delete any project. A missing or unknown id also leaves `user` null or undefined, so `user.isAdmin` throws.

findings.description: A production payments API token is hardcoded in source and committed to version control. Anyone with repo access can use it, and it should be rotated.

If PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN is unset, the code now silently falls back to the hardcoded prod token instead of failing. A misconfigured dev, test, or staging environment would send real charges to production.

spurious.description: If PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN is unset, the code now silently falls back to the hardcoded prod token instead of failing. A misconfigured dev, test, or staging environment would send real charges to production.

findings.description: The bare `except Exception: pass` swallows every save failure with no logging or re-raise. If repo.save fails (e.g. DB outage or constraint violation), orders are silently dropped. The function returns a lower count, and the caller can't tell a partial sync from a complete one. Log the exception, and either re-raise or report the failures.

orders_with_customers loads all orders unbounded and then calls session.get(Customer, ...) per order, an N+1 pattern. session.get hits the identity map only for already-loaded customers, so with many distinct customers it issues one query each. Use a single join or joinedload/selectinload instead.

missed.description: The cached C image is only dropped when the size changes, not the mode. An MPO whose frame 0 is L and frame 1 is RGB/CMYK at the same size decodes wide pixels into the stale narrow buffer: native out-of-bounds write (GHSA-v9pv-5gc8-w2m6, fixed in Pillow 13.0.0).

findings.description: When the base_url has a query string and the merged URL also has one (e.g. build_request('GET', '/users?a=1') with base 'https://x/get?data=1'), merge_url.raw_path already contains '?a=1'. The code appends another '?' + base_query, giving 'users?a=1?data=1'. The query is malformed: the base param is folded into a's value, and the request's own params are mixed with it.

Path traversal: `name` comes straight from the URL and is joined to NOTES_DIR with no validation, and the allowlist check against list_notes() was removed. A request like `/notes/../../etc/passwd` or an absolute-style path passes `is_file()` and the server returns that file's contents. This allows reading any file the process can access.

The `name` argument is interpolated directly into the SQL string, so it allows SQL injection. An input like `' UNION SELECT id, password FROM users --` changes the query and can expose or alter data. Use a parameterized query instead: `conn.execute("... LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

`count // per_page` uses floor division, so it drops a partial last page. For example, 25 items with per_page=20 returns 1 instead of 2, and 5 items returns 0. It needs ceiling division, e.g. `(count + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

`getUser` is async, as `getProjects` awaits it, but it isn't awaited here. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined. Every delete request, including those from real admins, gets a 403, and `removeProject` never runs.

The admin check depends on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user id can delete any project. The handler also never checks that the project exists or belongs to the caller.

spurious.description: The admin check depends on the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone who sends an admin's user id can delete any project. The handler also never checks that the project exists or belongs to the caller.

If PAYMENTS_API_TOKEN is unset, the code now falls back silently to the hardcoded prod token instead of failing. A misconfigured dev or staging environment will then make real charges with production credentials.

findings.description: `except Exception: pass` swallows every error from `repo.save`, including DB outages and constraint violations. Failed orders are dropped with no log or re-raise. The function returns a smaller count and the caller can't tell the sync was partial, so orders are silently lost. Log the exception (the module already defines `log`), and either re-raise or report the failures.

N+1 query: for every order, `session.get(Customer, ...)` can issue a separate SELECT for each distinct customer not already in the identity map. The query also loads all orders with no limit. With many orders this means thousands of queries. Use a single join, such as `session.query(Order, Customer).join(Customer, Customer.id == Order.customer_id)`, or eager loading.

findings.description: If the base_url has a query and the request URL also has one, e.g. base `https://h/get?data=1` with `build_request('GET', '/users?x=1')`, the merged raw_path becomes `/get/users?x=1?data=1`. The request's own query is corrupted (`x` becomes `1?data=1`) and the base query is not merged properly. The two queries need to be combined with `&`.

The allowlist check was replaced with `NOTES_DIR / name`, which is only an `is_file()` test. A request such as `GET /notes/../../etc/passwd`, or an absolute path like `/notes//etc/passwd`, resolves outside NOTES_DIR and is served. The path is not normalised, resolved or confined to NOTES_DIR, and any readable file is exposed. It also no longer requires a `.txt` suffix.

The `name` value is interpolated straight into the SQL string with an f-string, so it allows SQL injection. An input such as `' UNION SELECT id, password FROM users --` can read arbitrary data, and `'` alone breaks the query. Use a parameterized query instead: `conn.execute("... WHERE name LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))`.

`count // per_page` uses floor division, so a partial last page is dropped. For example, 25 items with per_page=20 returns 1 page instead of 2, and 5 items returns 0 pages. Use ceiling division: `(count + per_page - 1) // per_page`.

`getUser` is async, as `getProjects` shows by awaiting it, but it isn't awaited here. `user` is a Promise, so `user.isAdmin` is always undefined and every call returns 403, even for admins. Delete never works.

The caller's identity comes from the client-supplied `x-user-id` header with no authentication. Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone can send an admin's user id and delete any project. If `getUser` returns null for an unknown id, `user.isAdmin` throws and the request returns a 500 instead of a 401 or 403.

Once the missing `await` is fixed, anyone can send an admin's user id and delete any project. If `getUser` returns null for an unknown id, `user.isAdmin` throws and the request returns a 500 instead of a 401 or 403.

findings.description: `except Exception: pass` swallows every error from `repo.save` with no logging or re-raise. If the DB is down or an order is invalid, orders are silently dropped and the caller only sees a lower count. It can't tell a partial failure from success, and the cause is lost. Log the exception (a `log` is already defined) and either re-raise or report the failures.

N+1 query: session.get(Customer, order.customer_id) is called for every order, and the unbounded session.query(Order).all() loads every order. For large tables this issues thousands of queries (the identity map only caches repeat customer IDs). Use a single join, e.g. session.query(Order, Customer).join(Customer, Order.customer_id == Customer.id), or eager loading.

missed.description: The cached C image is only dropped when the size changes, not the mode. An MPO whose frame 0 is L and frame 1 is RGB/CMYK at the same size decodes wide pixels into the stale narrow buffer: native out-of-bounds write (GHSA-v9pv-5gc8-w2m6, fixed in Pillow 13.0.0).

findings.description: When the base URL has a query and the request URL also has one, the code appends `?` + base_query after a path that already contains a query. For example, `build_request('GET', '/users?x=1')` with base `.../get?data=1` gives `/get/users?x=1?data=1`, a malformed query. The two queries should be merged with `&`, or the request's query should take precedence.

The allowlist check against list_notes() was replaced with a bare is_file() on NOTES_DIR / name. A request like GET /notes/../../etc/passwd (or an absolute-looking name, or any non-.txt file in notes/) passes is_file() and read_bytes() returns arbitrary files from the server. The name needs to be resolved and checked to be inside NOTES_DIR and to match the listed *.txt notes.
